title: Eviction loop + batching thrash sleuth log
content:
Summary:

This is a working sleuth log from the on-call team for a recurring host-level memory thrash that surfaced as a tail-latency spike and large numbers of microbatch failures across a subset of serving hosts. Behavior looked like repeated eviction cycles (host-level) coinciding with batch-queue starvation and large numbers of tiny microbatches being scheduled.

High-level impact:
- 03:12–04:05 UTC on 2026-02-27: elevated 95/99th latency for text-generation routes (models: rwd-1.3-quantv2, rwd-chat-medium)
- Increased error rate ~2.8% (transient timeouts, OOM+restarts on affected pods)
- Customer-facing degradation for a handful of mid-tier tenants (dedicated pools)

Why this doc exists:
- Capture timeline, commands run, hypotheses and evidence, temporary mitigations, and a first draft of a runbook entry to alert and respond to future occurrences.

Timeline (live notes):
- 03:10 UTC: Alert fires - avg host evictions / min spikes from 0.2 -> 3.5 on a subset of hosts in pool us-west-2-dedicated-4.
- 03:12 UTC: On-call (Marcus) pulls top: heap growth visible on host gpu-34, vGPU memory oscillation between 6.2GB -> 12.7GB before eviction.
- 03:18 UTC: Discovered microbatch queue depth on the host dropping to near-zero repeatedly while global request rate was steady.
- 03:22 UTC: Correlated with kv-index increase metric: kv_index_entries{host=~"gpu-.*"} increased by ~8x over 30m on affected hosts.
- 03:30 UTC: Tried soft mitigation: set runtime.dyn.prefetch_enabled = false on a canary host; observed reduced eviction frequency after 3 min.
- 03:38 UTC: Rolled back the rwd-1.3-quantv2 rollout that had started earlier that day to stable variant on affected pool (rollback via rollout manager).
- 03:44 UTC: Drained and rebooted two most impacted hosts; memory usage stabilized and latency returned to baseline by ~03:55 UTC.

Immediate observations / evidence:
- Memory growth pattern: slow linear climb during bursty seq-length 1024 traffic that caused per-entry KV meta to expand (observed via custom per-request kv-meta-size metric).
- Eviction API logs show repeated allocate->evict->retry loop rather than a single sustained eviction followed by stability. Sequence suggests wasted work and batch starvation.
- Batch lifecycle traces show many tiny microbatches (1–3 requests) with enqueue/dequeue churn; continuous batching heuristics seemed to stop coalescing.
- A recent change in kv-index compaction (PR #987) altered in-memory slot representation for compacted entries; memory-per-entry under certain clients (long prompt + many prefixes) increased unexpectedly.

Hypothesis (current):
A regression in the kv-index compaction component increases per-entry memory under specific sequence-length and prefix patterns. The memory increase pushes host memory over the eviction threshold repeatedly. Eviction triggers internal cache invalidation that interacts poorly with the continuous batching scheduler (scheduler sees many cache-miss / prefetch attempts, which re-populate tiny entries), producing a thrash pattern: eviction → prefetch → small batch scheduling → more entries → eviction. The net effect is batch starvation and high tail latency.

Commands / queries used during triage (for runbook later):
- Prometheus queries:
  - topk(10, increase(eviction_count[5m]))
  - sum by(host) (kv_index_entries)
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(batch_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))
- Host-level checks:
  - kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-34
  - ssh gpu-34 -- sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 500 | grep -i eviction
  - /opt/runtime/bin/observe-kv --host gpu-34 --dump-metric kv_meta_size --top 30

Temporary mitigations applied (ordered):
1) Disable prefetch on a canary host (runtime dynconfig): observed near-instant reduction in eviction churn; flag left off for 45m while watching.
2) Rollback quantized model variant rwd-1.3-quantv2 to rwd-1.3-stable for affected pools to stop the new allocation pattern.
3) Drain and reboot the two highest-eviction hosts to clear fragmented allocations and stabilize host-local state.
4) Increase eviction threshold (eviction.watermark.percent) by 3% for the pool as a stop-gap; later reverted after stabilization.

Why the mitigations helped:
- Disabling prefetch reduced write-path pressure on KV index so entries stopped ramping up.
- Rollback removed the code-path that created larger per-kv entries under this traffic shape.
- Reboots cleared in-process fragmentation / leaked metadata on the host.

Post-incident artifacts captured:
- heap profiles + jemalloc stats from drained hosts (uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident/2026-02-27/eviction-loop-profiles/)
- batch traces for affected time window (trace IDs saved in linked artifacts)
- runtime logs extracted and trimmed to 200MB for team review

First-pass root cause (tentative):
- A change in kv-index compaction (PR #987) introduced a defensive metadata field that in pathological prefix-arrays duplicated certain strings instead of referencing interned slices. Under long-seq traffic with frequent prefix overlaps, per-entry overhead jumped, causing hosts to hit eviction watermark earlier and repeatedly. The design assumption that compaction would reduce resident memory under all patterns proved false for this workload.

Longer-term fixes proposed:
- Revert the offending allocation pattern in KV compaction and add unit tests that generate the pathological prefix-array cases. (Owner: Diego Ramos, ETA: 2026-03-15)
- Add a per-host guardrail metric: kv_meta_size_per_entry and an alert when average > 1.5x baseline for 5m. (Owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-01)
- Add an automatic runtime fallback for pools: if eviction_rate > X and batch_coalescing_rate < Y, force prefetch=false and promote to emergency config until operator clears. (Owner: eng-serving-runtime, ETA: 2026-04-01)
- Improve continuous batching health signals: track microbatch_size_distribution and surface a throttling backoff when average batch size < 4 and request rate > threshold. (Owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-08)
- Add chaos test(s) to e2e harness to simulate kv-index pathologies and verify eviction + batching interactions. (Owner: SRE QA, ETA: 2026-03-22)

Runbook draft (detect → mitigate → escalate):
1) Detection:
   - Alert: eviction_rate_per_host > 1/min for 3 hosts in a pool OR batch_coalescing_rate < 0.5 for 5m + 99th latency > baseline * 2.
   - Run detection query template (prometheus snippets above).
2) Triage:
   - Identify affected hosts, model variants active on those hosts, and recent deploys (last 1h).
   - Capture heap profile and kv_meta_size snapshot.
3) Immediate mitigation:
   - Toggle runtime.dyn.prefetch_enabled=false on a single canary host, watch for 3–5 min.
   - If improvement, roll toggle to remaining hosts in pool.
   - If no improvement, initiate model-variant rollback for recently rolled models in that pool.
4) Stabilize:
   - Drain and reboot at most 2 hosts simultaneously, verify memory stabilizes before returning to traffic.
5) Escalation:
   - If mitigations fail after 30m, page eng-serving-runtime on-call and product incident lead.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did the compaction regression only surface in certain pools? (hypothesis: client prompt shape differences + quota/tenant skew)
- Is there an interaction with host-level allocator (jemalloc arenas) causing fragmentation amplification? Need allocator expert to review heap profiles.
- Should we consider throttling prefetch concurrency instead of a full toggle?

Action items (short-lived):
- [Diego] Revert PR #987 and run the pathological prefix-array unit test. (ETA 2026-03-15)
- [Priya] Create and wire alert for kv_meta_size_per_entry. (ETA 2026-03-01)
- [Aisha] Implement microbatch_size_distribution metric and dashboard (ETA 2026-03-08).
- [Marcus] Draft final runbook entry and ensure runbook is discoverable from SRE on-call pager. (ETA 2026-03-03)

Notes for postmortem write-up:
- Timeline + root cause + mitigations and why they worked.
- Customers impacted and communication timeline.
- Code-level fix, tests added, and regression prevention plan.
- RCA follow-through: allocator review + compaction audits.

Appendix (links and quick references):
- Query templates (prometheus): /confluence/snippets/eviction-runbook-queries
- Heap profile storage: s3://redwood-incident/2026-02-27/
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Pager history: PagerDuty incident 2026-02-27-5032

End of sleuth log.
